title: The normalized source-isomorphism comparisons commute with the second mate
statement: Use the unchanged scheme, functor, adjunction and ordinary-base-change hypotheses of lem-sc-right-adjoint-mate-scheme-iso-transport-mate, assume r is an isomorphism, and supply natural isomorphisms φ and ψ for a,b along e and d,b′ along r, each satisfying the counit normalization of lem-sc-scheme-iso-right-adjoint-normalized. For every supplied ordinary invertibility family hβf, define s by canonical pullback composition along r and pullback.fst f g, the first projection equation, inverse composition along pullback.fst f′ g and e.hom, and pullback of φK. Then s.hom≫the ambient f′ second mate at K equals the r-pullback of the ambient f second mate at K followed by ψ at LgK. This is an equality for specified comparisons; it supplies neither comparison existence nor an arrow isomorphism.

source.place: Tag 0ATR, composite adjunction and conjugate calculation; Tag 0D5S, canonical pullback composition

proof.text: Transpose ordinary base change under the pinned adjunctions. The two projection equations and he identify the transposes via canonical pullback composition associativity. Injectivity of the Hom equivalence gives transport of ordinary base change.

The counit normalizations for φ and ψ imply the transported unit identities by adjunction transposition. Expand the fixed second mate into its base unit, inverse conjugate and upper counit. Transport the conjugate of the preceding ordinary comparison and its inverse, substitute the normalization identities, reassociate, and cancel comparison inverse pairs. The result is exactly s.hom≫mate′=Lr(mate)≫ψ. No second mate is inverted.

proof_origin.note: Categorical specialization; normalized endpoint comparisons are proved in Lean, and the remaining square is isolated.
